column2: 최근 외곽 지역을 중심으로 노숙자 실종 신고가 잇따르고 있습니다. 경찰은 단순 이동 가능성도 배제하지 않고 있으나...
column3: Recently, there has been a series of missing person reports involving homeless individuals, primarily in the outskirts. The police are not ruling out the possibility that they have simply relocated, but...

column2: 요새 흉흉하네요. 이럴 때일수록 우리 일거리는 늘어서 좋지만 말이에요.
column3: Things are pretty grim lately. But hey, times like these mean more work for us.

column2: 남들이 실종된다는데 그게 할 소리냐?
column3: People are going missing, and that's what you have to say?

column2: 사건이 없으면 탐정이고 경찰이고 무슨 소용이에요? 지금까지 한 일이라곤 고양이 찾아주기, 바람난 남편 뒤쫓기, 잃어버린 반지 찾기였잖아요.
column3: What good is a detective or the police without a case? All you've done so far is find lost cats, tail cheating husbands, and track down missing rings.

column2: 그 반지는 하수구에서 찾았다. 내 직업적 존엄성도 같이 빠져 있었고.
column3: I found that ring in a sewer. My professional dignity was down there right along with it.

column2: 셜록 홈즈도 처음부터 대단한 사건만 맡은 건 아니에요. 이를테면 주홍색 연구에서...
column3: Sherlock Holmes didn't start out with huge cases either. For instance, in A Study in Scarlet...

column2: 멈춰. 전화 온다.
column3: Stop. The phone's ringing.

column2: 전화벨이 울린다. 주인공은 귀찮다는 듯 수화기를 든다.
column3: The phone rings. The protagonist picks up the receiver, looking annoyed.

column2: 네, 탐정 사무소입니다. 고양이면 끊으세요.
column3: Yes, this is the detective agency. If it's about a cat, hang up.

column2: 산속에 있는 저택을 조사해주셨으면 합니다.
column3: I'd like you to investigate a mansion in the mountains.

column2: 지도에도 없는 저택이라면 대체로 사유지입니다. 전직 경찰로서 불법 침입 의뢰는 안 받습니다.
column3: A mansion that isn't even on the map is usually private property. As a former cop, I don't take on trespassing jobs.

column2: 선금은 두 배로 드리죠.
column3: I'll double the advance payment.

column2: ...방금 금액, 원화 맞습니까? 0 하나 더 붙이신 거 아니고요?
column3: ...That amount you just mentioned, is that in Won? You didn't accidentally add an extra zero, did you?

column2: 통화가 끝난 뒤, 조수가 메모지를 들여다본다.
column3: After the call, the assistant peeks at the notepad.

column2: 히익. 무슨 의뢰인데 돈을 이렇게 줘요?
column3: Yikes. What kind of job pays this much?

column2: 사람 없는 저택 조사.
column3: Investigating an abandoned mansion.

column2: 아, 거기요? 귀신 나온다는 데 아니에요? 물론 전 귀신 같은 건 안 믿지만요. 그런데 그 저택, 예전에 봉사 단체 사람들이 썼다고 들었어요. 변론하는 자였나?
column3: Oh, that place? Isn't it supposed to be haunted? Not that I believe in ghosts, of course. But I heard that mansion used to be used by a volunteer group. 'The Advocates', was it?

column2: 변론하는 자?
column3: The Advocates'?

column2: 노숙자들 돕고, 기부하고, 기사도 꽤 났던 곳이요. 이름은 좀 이상하지만 좋은 사람들 같던데요?
column3: They helped the homeless, made donations, and got quite a bit of press. The name's a bit weird, but they seemed like good people.

column2: 요새 노숙자 실종 사건이 늘었다고 했지.
column3: You mentioned earlier that missing person cases involving the homeless have been on the rise lately.

column2: 설마요?
column3: You don't think...?

column2: 늘 하던 대로 해. 네가 먼저 사전 답사하고, 주변 소문이랑 출입 가능 경로만 확인해.
column3: Do what you always do. Scout the place first, gather some local rumors, and figure out the access routes.

column2: 넵. 금방 갔다 올게요.
column3: Got it. I'll be back soon.

column2: 조수는 돌아오지 않는다. 하루, 사흘, 일주일이 지난다. 연락은 끊기고, 주인공의 손에는 조수가 남긴 메모만 남는다.
column3: The assistant does not return. A day passes, then three, then a week. All contact is lost, leaving the protagonist with only the memo the assistant left behind.

column2: 일주일... 길어도 사흘이면 돌아오던 녀석이.
column3: A week... He usually comes back in three days at most.

column2: 주인공은 과거 동료를 잃었던 순간을 떠올린다. 총성, 인질, 자신의 망설임, 그리고 쓰러진 동료.
column3: The protagonist recalls the moment he lost his former partner. Gunshots, hostages, his own hesitation, and his partner falling to the ground.

column2: 또 잃을 순 없어. 이번에도 가만히 있으면... 이번엔 진짜 끝이야.
column3: I can't lose someone again. If I just sit here and do nothing... this time, it's really over.

column2: 주인공은 코트를 집어 들고 저택으로 향한다.
column3: The protagonist grabs his coat and heads to the mansion.

column2: 주인공은 조수의 마지막 메모를 다시 접어 주머니에 넣는다.
column3: He folds the assistant's last memo and slips it into his pocket.

column2: 기다려라. 이번엔 내가 늦지 않을 테니까.
column3: Just wait. I won't be late this time.

column2: 현관문은 너무 쉽게 열린다.
column3: The front door opens far too easily.

column2: 문이 열린다? 이건 친절이 아니라 함정이지.
column3: It's unlocked? That's not hospitality... that's a trap.
